newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR WANTS TIME FOR YOUNGSTERS TO DEVELOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR WANTS TIME FOR YOUNGSTERS TO DEVELOP.

text.p: India's captain Sachin Tendulkar has asked for time for his young squad to develop in the wake of their crushing defeats in the first two tests in South Africa.
With the third and final test remaining, the Indians have to come up with a solution to their batting frailty against the South African pace attack and their own bowling deficiencies.
Tendulkar told reporters his side must now look forward after the 282-run defeat in the second test in Cape Town on Monday following the 328-run drubbing in the first test in Durban.
"We have to leave all this behind us and concentrate on the third test and see how we can come up with a better performance," Tendulkar said."All 11 of us have to contribute much more."
It is difficult to see where India can make sudden improvements.

In three of their test innings in South Africa they have been bowled out for 100, 66 and 144 and in the fourth they were 58 for five before centuries from Tendulkar (169) and Azharuddin (115) hauled them to a follow-on saving 359.
Those two innings are the only occasions Indian batsmen have reached 50 whereas South Africa have so far recorded 11 half-centuries.

Although the home players have found Javagal Srinath (11 wickets) and Venkatesh Prasad (13) difficult opponents -- rated as "two of the best in the world" by South African captain Hansie Cronje -- India's support bowling has been poor.

Leg-spinner Anil Kumble has been ineffective with only four wickets from 105 overs -- South African wrist-spinner Paul Adams has five from 34.2 -- while change seamers David Johnson and Doda Ganesh have each played one test and contributed three wickets between them.

"Ganesh and Johnson are both youngsters," said Tendulkar. "They have just played three tests between them and you can't expect miracles from them. It's a young side and they will learn the accuracy you need in a third seamer but it will take time."
India's batting problems start at the top where their opening partnerships to date have been two, two, seven and seven and they have yet to score more than 50 with fewer than four wickets down.
"It has been happening to South Africa as well," said Tendulkar. "But what is important is that the other opener hangs in there and sees to it that he gets a big score.
"I have seen a lot in the batting of Ganguly, Dravid and Laxman to face the future with confidence."
The Cape Town test was hailed as the best in South Africa's history by United Cricket Board managing director Ali Bacher.
"The presence of President Mandela and Archbishop Tutu combined with the quality of cricket has to make this the most joyous moment in our cricket history," Bacher told the Cape Times newspaper.
The match was watched by a Newlands record crowd of 74,577.
India now have a limited overs day-night match in Kimberley and a three-day game against Free State before the third test in Johannesburg starting on January 16.
